| Component | Weight | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Lab completion — Labs 1–6, run on your own checkout | 50% | a checkpoint commit and a `BENCHMARKS.md` entry per lab |
| Practical assessments PA-1 and PA-2 | 10% | artefacts plus notes |
| Capstone project and evaluation report | 40% | the [capstone rubric](capstone.qmd#the-seven-sections) |

The quiz below is **not scored**. It runs on Day 4 as a fifteen-minute check you
mark yourself, and it is discussed immediately afterwards — the discussion is the
point, not the number.

The labs strand (60%) and the project with its report (40%) match the catalogue
assessment: *labs; an LLM application project with an evaluation report*. Each
module is theory then a lab notebook, and the lab is worked on your own checkout —
its numbers land in your `BENCHMARKS.md` and become the capstone's evidence.

Badge issuance requires ≥ 70 overall **and** capstone ≥ 70 **and** a green safety
suite at submission **and** no academic-integrity flags. Identical golden-set edits
and copied report numbers are checked across repositories, and the holdout run
exposes fabricated results.

## Practical assessments

### PA-1 — repair a broken branch (30 minutes, end of Day 2)

You are given a Murshid branch with three defects: a tool description that
misroutes, a schema relaxed to `str`, and a missing repair loop. Restore extraction
pass rate ≥ 95% and `make tool-smoke` green.

| Scored on | Weight |
|---|---|
| Diagnosis notes — what you found, and how you knew | 40% |
| The fixes | 40% |
| Verification evidence — the re-run numbers | 20% |

The diagnosis notes carry more weight than the fixes on purpose. Anybody can
restore a schema; the skill is reading a corpus report and knowing which of three
things it is telling you.

### PA-2 — review a pull request (30 minutes, end of Day 3)

You are given a PR that "improves" a prompt: friendlier tone, **−9 points
groundedness on the Arabic slice**, safety green. Write the review: what may merge,
what must change, and what evidence you demand before it does.

| Scored on | Weight |
|---|---|
| Triage correctness — is this blocking, and why | 50% |
| Use of slice evidence rather than the average | 30% |
| Review tone and actionability | 20% |

A review that says "this looks fine, tone is subjective" fails. So does one that
says "rejected" with no evidence and no path forward.

## Quiz bank

Twenty questions covering the week. **None of this is scored** — use it as a
self-check before the capstone. If a question makes you hesitate, the module that
answers it is named above the group.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Module 1 — architecture

**Q1.** Rank single-call, workflow, router and agentic loop by failure surface, and
state the escalation rule.

**Q2.** Why must application code never import a provider SDK directly?

**Q3.** True or false: streaming reduces total generation time.

**Q4.** A human does not wait for this response. What does that imply?

**Q5.** Name the three governors that bound an agentic loop.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Module 2 — APIs and open weights

**Q6.** Name two of the load-bearing differences between the OpenAI-compatible and
Anthropic Messages dialects.

**Q7.** Why does temperature 0 not make outputs reproducible, and where does
determinism actually come from?

**Q8.** `finish_reason="length"` — what happened, and what must the application do?

**Q9.** An Arabic prompt tokenises 1.9× its English twin on your route. Name two
engineering consequences — and one reason the ratio might be wrong next quarter.

**Q10.** Which two vLLM ideas make self-hosting economical?
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Modules 3 and 4 — structure, tools, guards

**Q11.** JSON mode versus strict schema mode — what does each guarantee, and what
does neither guarantee?

**Q12.** Who executes a tool call, and why is that the security model?

**Q13.** The model supplies a `national_id` argument for a booking. What decides
whose booking it is?

**Q14.** Why is prompt injection unsolvable in the SQL-injection sense?

**Q15.** Which two numbers must every guard change report, and why the pair?

**Q16.** What is a canary token, and which wall uses it?

**Q17.** Why do prompts get new versions instead of in-place edits?
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Modules 5 and 6 — evaluation and cost

**Q18.** Name the three golden-set splits and the reason for the third.

**Q19.** Which assert types may gate safety, and where do judges fit?

**Q20.** What breaks provider prompt caching, and what discipline prevents it?

**Bonus.** Write the one sentence that governs every optimisation in Module 6.
:::

## Wrap-up

Every capstone requirement maps back to the module that taught it, and that is the
golden thread whole: every component built during the week is running in the
application you just demonstrated.

Forward pointers: **SDA-AIE-214** adds retrieval to this exact pipeline — the
guarded pipeline and the eval harness grow retrieval metrics on the same skeleton.
**SDA-AIE-215** turns the adaptation question (prompt versus retrieval versus
fine-tune) into strategy. **SDA-AIE-312/313/315** build LLMOps, security and
solution architecture on this substrate.

The last word:

> The model will be replaced within a year. Every discipline in this course
> survives that replacement — and the harness is how you will prove the replacement
> is an upgrade.
